title: NocoBase Studio user guide
description: Deploy Studio, connect computers and team agents, create a project, and configure CI previews with this step-by-step guide.
heading: Your workspace.
intro: Deploy, connect, collaborate, and deliver. Bring your server, Coding Agents, and repositories together, all the way to your first project preview.

chapters.title: Deploy Studio
chapters.summary: Prepare a server with internet access, then deploy Studio.
chapters.html:
The server needs access to the image registry and related external services. Before deploying, prepare server access, a domain, and registry credentials, and check the existing reverse proxy and persistent data directories.

A deployment prompt for your agent

This example uses a placeholder domain and deployment path. Replace the server IP, directory, and domain before running it.

Deployment prompt
Connect over SSH to root@YOUR_SERVER_IP and install and deploy NocoBase Studio.

Deployment configuration:
- Docker image: pkg-v3.nocobase.com/nocobase/studio:latest
- Registry token: provided privately
- Deployment directory: /root/deploy/apps/studio
- Public URL: https://studio.example.com/main/
- Studio base path: /main
- Existing Caddy Compose file: /root/deploy/docker-compose.yml

Requirements:
1. Inspect existing deployments, Docker networks, and Caddy configuration first, without disrupting other services.
2. For an existing Studio instance, preserve the database, uploads, and administrator account. For a new installation, use nocobase as the administrator, generate a random password, and save it in a server configuration file with mode 600.
3. Configure persistent storage, automatic container restarts, and Caddy reverse proxying with HTTPS.
4. Use unique container names and network aliases to avoid conflicts with other Studio instances.
5. Use the same /main site URL for Studio, the CLI, agents, and repository CI. Update Git callbacks and webhook URLs accordingly.
6. Verify container health, HTTPS access, administrator sign-in, and data persistence after a restart.
7. Report the deployed version, URL, configuration file locations, how to retrieve the password, and verification results.
Use the complete site URL everywhere

The Studio entry point in this example is https://studio.example.com/main/. Use this address for the CLI, computer connections, runtimes, and CI, including /main.

Ready whenHTTPS works, the administrator can sign in, and data survives a container restart.

chapters.title: Configure the Studio CLI
chapters.summary: Let a local Coding Agent manage Studio projects and issues from the command line.
chapters.html:
1. Open the account menu in the upper-right corner and select Use Studio in your agent.
  2. Select Copy setup instructions in the dialog and give the prompt to your local Coding Agent.
  1. Check node --version and npm first. The CLI requires Node.js 24 or later.
  2. Follow the prompt to install the CLI and run the login command. Open the displayed URL in your browser, enter the verification code, and authorize the connection.
  3. After signing in, check your identity and permissions, read the command documentation, and install the CLI skill.
Checks after signing in
nb-studio whoami
nb-studio docs
nb-studio skills install
Copy fresh instructions from your current site

Screenshots help you locate the controls. Installation links and verification codes can expire, so use instructions generated by the current site. If you connect to multiple Studio instances, check that the active profile points to the intended site before running commands.

Ready whenwhoami shows your identity and permissions on the intended site, and your agent has the CLI skill installed.

chapters.title: Connect My agents
chapters.summary: Connect your computer to Studio and use its Coding Agents from your browser.
chapters.html:
1. Open My agents and select Connect your computer.
  2. Copy the connection prompt and give it to an agent on the computer you want to connect.

After installation and browser sign-in, follow the instructions to install a background service that keeps the computer online. For a temporary connection, use nb-studio acp start. In My computers, confirm that the computer is online and check which Coding Agents are available.

Computer directory access

Access to the entire user directory is allowed by default. You can adjust the permitted folders in My computers.

Ready whenYour computer is online, and the selected Coding Agent has completed its own authorization and can start a session.

chapters.title: Configure runtimes and team agents
chapters.summary: Connect a runtime, enable agents, and select an execution agent for the project manager.
chapters.html:
1. Add a runtime

Open Agent team → Runtimes, select Add runtime, and choose Personal or Team based on who will use it.

Select the Coding Agent tools you plan to use on the machine and set Max concurrent runs. This controls the maximum number of simultaneous runs; adjust it to fit machine resources and model usage limits. Generate the installation command, run it on the target machine, and authorize the selected tools.

2. Configure and enable agents

Once the runtime is online, open Agent team → Agents and select Fill in and enable for each discovered agent to complete its configuration and enable it.

3. Choose an execution agent for the project manager

Open Project manager. Under The agent it runs with → First choice, select an enabled, available agent. Optionally select a Fallback, then save.

The project manager needs configuration too

Bringing the runtime online is only one step. Enable the team agents and choose an execution agent for the project manager. On a new site, the project manager may be unable to take on work until this is configured.

Ready whenThe runtime is online, team agents are available, and the project manager’s First choice is saved.

chapters.title: Connect Git
chapters.summary: Connect a code repository for your projects.
chapters.html:
Open Settings → Git and select Add connection. The interface supports GitHub and GitLab. Follow the instructions for your chosen platform to complete the connection.

Confirm that the connected account or organization can access the target repository. If Studio will create a repository, also confirm that the connection has the required permissions.

Ready whenThe Git connection is available, and you can select the intended account or repository when creating a project.

chapters.title: Create a project
chapters.summary: Prepare your repository and the permissions needed to configure CI, then create your Studio project.
chapters.html:
Have the project’s Git repository, target branch, and permissions for repository CI ready. Open Projects, select New project, and follow the wizard to choose a Git connection and code source.

Choose an existing repository or create a new one for the project. If code needs to be initialized, select an available execution agent. Once the project is created, continue to the next chapter to configure CI and previews.

Ready whenThe project is created and linked to the correct repository and code source.

chapters.title: Set up CI and previews
chapters.summary: Report repository build results to Studio and configure previews for pull requests.
chapters.html:
1. Open the project’s CI wizard

Open the project’s Settings → Deployment and select Set up CI.

2. Set the trigger and application details

Choose Pull request, Push to a branch, or Tag as needed, then enter the environment, application directory, and App ID. The example uses Pull request and a preview environment. If the application is in the repository root, set Directory to ..

3. Add CI configuration to the repository

  1. Use the generated template or copy Prompt for your agent to add the CI configuration files to the repository. For GitHub, these usually go in .github/workflows/. For GitLab, follow the wizard to include them from .gitlab-ci.yml.
  2. Configure repository secrets as instructed by the current wizard. The example secret is NB_STUDIO_API_KEY. Use the key and site URL generated for your current project.
  3. Commit the configuration and trigger a matching build. Return to Deployment to check the first CI report and preview result.
How task previews map to applications

When a task’s pull request triggers CI, the wizard’s example creates a preview application named <app-id>-pr-<number> and removes it when the PR is merged or closed. Configure project CI and previews first, then use a PR to verify automatic creation and cleanup.

Ready whenCI reports successfully, the preview URL is accessible, and the PR’s build and preview status appear in Studio.
